_comment: THE FALSE FAIL BESIDE THE FALSE PASS, LEGALLY PLACED (task-8532dae7b075f4b3). One row the prior census remembers as open has been re-parented out of the epic and onto the successor’s FIRST WAVE — a grandchild of the successor, which is where a successor epic with waves actually puts a forwarded row. `parent_id` is one field, so the row is under the successor ONLY and nowhere in `children`. A predicate that reads the successor’s DIRECT roster only cannot see it: the row is charged as a FILING EVENT, NO SEAL, over a row that HAS a forwarding address. The committed file walks the successor’s subtree, RE-HOMES it and seals. Until task-8532dae7b075f4b3 this fixture listed the same _id in BOTH `children` and the wave’s subtree — a row with two parents, which the ledger cannot produce and which the predicate now refuses as FIXTURE-TWO-PARENTS.
